source: https://ddayboards.com.au/ (official Avada portfolio lineup — six named production models with unique product-fronts and first-party shaper notes; excludes gallery Instagram, contact forms, and custom deposits)

brands.name: DDay Boards
brands.short_description: Custom surfboards hand-shaped in Victoria for down-the-line drive and controlled handling, from fish and eggs to twins and step-ups.

models.name: Fish-Twin Keel
models.description: Traditional fish-esque boards shaped for speed and performance, especially in smaller surf, and some of the most versatile boards in the DDay quiver. Smaller sizes are tuned with more performance-oriented rocker and bottom contours for beach break and mid-sized point surf. Longer variations are slightly detuned in contour and rocker for longer, more powerful down-the-line point breaks. A side-cut variation is also offered for a snappier feel and easier rail-to-rail transitions.

models.name: Mid Length Egg
models.description: Shaped as the answer to perfect but smaller days at Bells and Winkipop, with subtle spiral vee throughout and softer forgiving rails. Two versions: a speedier tracker outline with less tail curve and a more rounded-point nose, and an EVO-inspired outline with rounded nose and tail plus increased tail area and curve. A good bridge for advanced and beginner surfers moving down from a longboard or moving up in length.

models.name: Round Tail Twin
models.description: Built to make a longer board looser and more maneuverable. Occupies a similar niche to the speed-shape eggs but is more capable in better waves. Compared with the 2+1 eggs, these deliver instant acceleration and reduced resistance with no center fin, enabling a tighter turning arc for boards of equivalent length. A one-board-quiver solution for surfers happy to ride a longer board as their daily rider.

models.name: Gun Twin Swallow Tail
models.description: Designed to complement the round-tail twin with more rocker, a slimmer outline, a more pointed nose, a gun-like tail curve, a full foil, and boxier rails. A step-up equivalent for round-tail twin riders, or a higher-performance mid-length for surfers coming from a shortboard or smaller hybrid. Versatile in high-quality or hollow surf, and a strong travel or everyday option for riders who need extra help catching waves.

models.name: Single with Side Bites
models.description: Not strictly a 1970s single fin, but that description captures the design: extra volume, a strong central drive from the middle fin, and a lot of control. Best in good, long, down-the-line waves like Winkipop and Bells. A shortboard replacement in 3–6 ft surf when you want exceptional paddle power, sheer speed, and long arcing lines rather than top-to-bottom surfing. Niche, demanding, and built for surfers willing to invest the time to ride them well.

models.name: Step Ups
models.description: The most consistent boards in the DDay quiver over the last ten years, stripped back for function when the waves are exceptional. Two foils share almost identical design features: a traditional shortboard foil for surfers who want a board slightly longer than their shortboard while keeping a performance approach, and a fuller foil with a small beak for extra paddling assistance, more pushback, and drive on the open face in more challenging surf.
